name: iOS Simulator
description: Private iOS simulators: each task sees its own device in its sidebar tab, and the Simulators view manages them all. Persistent run switch; 15-minute idle shutdown keeps data. Requires macOS 15+, Apple Silicon, full Xcode and an iOS runtime. Built on open-source Baguette (tddworks, Apache-2.0).
whenToUse: Default for iOS Simulator work: install, launch and drive built apps on private devices; screenshot, wait, capture changes, read logs; live view in the task sidebar. Start with devices. Verify with real touches (tap/gesture), not AXe/idb or Xcode windows. heal needs consent.

environment.description: Call when creating a device or diagnosing the setup: checks macOS 15.0+ and Apple Silicon, then reads the bundled Baguette, Xcode, installed iOS runtimes and device types. Downloads nothing. With an existing device, go straight to devices.

devices.description: Call first: list this plugin's private devices and states, each with tasks (how many tasks use it) and thisTask (assigned to the current task). Reuse this task's device or a free one (tasks 0); never control Cindy embedded or Xcode default devices.

device.description: Manage private devices. create: new device from environment's runtime and deviceType (about 7–12 GB each); only when the task needs a clean device, another model or isolation. boot: start and wait for initialization (about 105 s; on timeout inspect state); screenshot=true also returns the screen once it settles. shutdown: stop, keeping data. rename: keeps data. erase: wipe all apps and data. delete: remove the device permanently. Use erase and delete only when the user asks. Subject to the run switch; devices stop after 15 idle minutes by default (not while a view is open or a tool is operating them).

app.description: App lifecycle. install: install a locally built simulator .app (absolute appPath; build it with the project's own Xcode workflow). Skips when identical to the installed app, syncs only changed files when few changed, and returns a job for long installs (wait with install_status). info: installed version, build and executable fingerprint; with appPath, matchesLocal says whether this build is the one installed. launch: start it (relaunches by default; arguments, env; screenshot=true also returns the screen once it settles) and open the live view in this task's sidebar; check viewer.previewOpened (view capabilities: see viewer). terminate; uninstall (deletes its data); open_url (deep link; if iOS asks to open another app, screenshot and tap the prompt). Compares content checksums; registration/signing changes require a full install.

screenshot.description: Capture the current screen. Supported Cindy hosts attach the image; older hosts, or images still over 130 KB after JPEG compression, return only path: open it with your image tool before acting. Upright as the user sees it, with screen corners and Dynamic Island; by default 1 pixel = 1 view point, so image coordinates go straight to tap and gesture. grid=true overlays a labelled grid; region crops a rectangle; scale 2–3 for detail (divide coordinates by scale).

describe_ui.description: Read the on-screen elements (accessibility tree). Default: a compact list in reading order with role, text, id, frame and center in view points (tap the center directly). Filter with query/role; x,y returns what is under a point; mode=full returns the whole tree. Games and custom-drawn UIs without accessibility get the text read off the screen instead (source=ocr), with positions; use screenshot for icons without text.

tap.description: Real touch tap through the simulator's system touch path: no window, works while the Mac is locked, and the app receives a finger touch. Target an element by text or id (optional role, nth); in games, text matches the words read off the screen. Or tap a view point x,y (if the screen turned since you looked, it asks you to look again instead of tapping the wrong place). count=2 double-taps; duration≥0.5 long-presses. Returns the new elements about 0.6 s later (observe=ui); observe=screenshot attaches a screenshot. Never inject events into the app process. until=text waits for that text to appear (next page, dialog) instead of guessing settle.

gesture.description: Swipes and multi-finger gestures, also real touches. kind: swipe (from→to, or direction up/down/left/right; up = finger moves up, content advances); drag (hold for hold seconds, then move to to: drag and drop, reordering); pinch (center, from_spread→to_spread); pan (two fingers by [dx,dy]); edge (system edges: bottom = Home/app switcher, top = Notification or Control Center); scroll_to (swipe until the text or id element is fully visible, or report the end). View points; observe as in tap.

type_text.description: Type into the focused field. text: method=auto (default) pastes in regular apps (exact, any language) and, in games without accessibility, types US-keyboard characters key by key (switching a Pinyin or similar input source to English); or force paste or type. keys sends keys such as Enter, Escape, Backspace, Tab, up, a, cmd+A or shift+Tab; clear=true empties the field first. Check focus first and observe the result. Key-by-key typing keeps the on-screen keyboard hidden; in games Enter may submit, so tap an empty area to only end editing. observe and until work as in tap. Key events make iOS treat a hardware keyboard as attached and hide the on-screen keyboard until the device restarts; to check what the keyboard covers, use method=touch (pastes through the edit menu by touch) after a boot. method=touch cannot be combined with clear=true or keys.

press.description: Hardware buttons: home, lock, power, volume-up, volume-down, action, app-switcher, swipe-to-app-switcher, swipe-to-home, pull-down-to-notification-center, pull-down-to-lock-screen; duration holds it. release-input only releases stuck keys and stops repeats; it restarts nothing and closes no app.

wait_for.description: Return once a condition holds (up to 90 s) instead of fixed sleeps and repeated screenshots. text or id appears (gone=true: disappears; in games, the text read off the screen); stable=seconds: the screen changes less than tolerance (percent of pixels, default 0.5) for that long, optionally only within region; log=regex: a matching line in the app's log (with bundleId). screenshot=true attaches the screen. If it does not happen: met=false, the reason and the current screen; for game animation, a suggested tolerance.

capture.description: Capture a change: start recording frames, run action (tool tap, gesture, press, type_text, open_url or app_launch with its args), keep going for seconds (≤15), drop duplicate frames and return one contact sheet in time order labelled in milliseconds, plus the frame files. For transitions, animations, brief toasts, loading and skeleton screens. Without action it records whatever changes. Supported Cindy hosts attach the contact sheet; older hosts, or sheets over 130 KB, return the sheet path: open it with your image tool. execution preserves the action outcome; actionError has code, message and execution. Never blindly repeat an uncertain action.

set_state.description: Change device state, several at once: orientation; posture for foldables (closed/open/flat or degrees); appearance light/dark; contrast; text_size (Dynamic Type); network (profile name, offline, clear or {latency, bandwidth, loss}; applies to apps launched afterwards); location {lat, lon} or clear; status_bar clean (9:41, full bars and battery, for screenshots) or clear; privacy {action grant/revoke/reset, service, bundleId} to pre-answer permission prompts. Returns the new screen size and orientation after orientation or posture changes. Changing a permission terminates that app; set it before launch.

logs.description: Read an app's recent log and crash reports. bundleId or process selects it; last_seconds defaults to 120; level error (errors and faults only), default, info or debug; match filters by regex. Includes this device's recent crash summaries for that process by default (exception, reason, crashed-thread frames).

heal.description: Explicit Baguette repair for iOS 27 input shadowed by Device Hub, using simctl on the private device set. Restarts SpringBoard and terminates running apps; call only after the user accepts that. Try press(release-input) first for stuck keys.

viewer.description: Open (open) or close (close) the device's live view in this task's sidebar. open returns previewOpened; confirm it before saying it is shown. close only stops the view; the device and app keep running. The page is user-operated: input, rotation, shake, screenshots (Desktop or clipboard), device switching and start/stop (stopping ends apps), and Baguette advanced tools: location and motion simulation, status bar and persistent network conditions, camera input, accessibility tree, logs and recording export (may contain app private data); map search and tiles go through the plugin's proxy to OpenStreetMap. Tell the user about these before opening; opening runs none of them. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
